title: Autoscaler label-filtering bug causes Private tenants to miss warmup reservations and hit burst shortfall
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Summary: Several Private deployment customers experienced sustained latency spikes and quota throttles during a February 9th regional traffic surge. Investigation showed affected tenants failed to acquire warmup reservations from reserved pools, exhausting their burst budget and causing customer-facing errors. This ticket tracks the discovery, root cause, hotfix, and follow-up mitigations.

Impact: Multi-tenant Private clusters in us-west-2 running dedicated reserved pools had ~12 tenants (mix of enterprise and mid-market) with repeated cold starts and degraded throughput for ~45 minutes. Customer severity: two P1 escalations (Enterprise A, Platform Integrator B) reporting SLA breaches and operational incidents.

Reproduction: Locally reproduced by toggling autoscaler label filtering to drop custom metadata key `private_deployment:true` in the warmup scoring pipeline, then simulating a warm burst of traffic from tenants that should have been pre-warmed. The autoscaler returned zero warm reservations for those tenants despite available headroom.

Root cause: A refactor in the autoscaler filters (PR 11827) introduced a new sanitization step that removed unknown metadata keys before warmup scoring. The sanitization incorrectly normalized keys using a whitelist that excluded tenant-level 'deployment_type' metadata (set to "private" at Customer onboarding). Warmup scoring therefore saw those tenants as "hosted"-eligible and applied stricter rate-based warmup heuristics that suppressed reservations. In short: label/key filtering removed the signal used to allocate reserved-warm slots for Private tenants.

Fix deployed: Hotfix PR 11894 reverses the sanitization change and adds explicit allowlist entries for deployment_type and private_deployment keys. Hotfix included unit tests and an integration test that runs a three-tenant warmup scenario. Merged and rolled out to staging 2025-02-13 03:00 UTC, and to production us-west-2 2025-02-13 06:15 UTC.

Mitigation and rollback path: We shipped an immediate autoscaler policy override API during the incident to force warmup reservations for affected tenants until the code fix rolled out. That override was revoked after the fix and validation.

Customer comms: Engineering-engaged on-call coordinated with Customer Success and sent interim status messages while the override was in effect. Post-deploy we notified Enterprise A and Platform Integrator B with root cause summary and mitigation steps.

Post-deploy validation: After rollout, warmup acquisition rate increased to baseline for Private tenants; burst-credit exhaustion events dropped to zero for the affected tenants within 12 minutes of the fix. Latency percentiles returned to pre-incident baselines within 25 minutes.

Telemetry changes: Added a dedicated telemetry counter `autoscaler.warmup.missing_deployment_signal` and a dashboard showing warmup reservation vs allocated headroom by `deployment_type`.

Follow-ups: 1) Add schema-driven metadata validation at tenant onboarding to prevent silenced keys. 2) Expand integration coverage for autoscaler policy tests to include Private/Hosted/Hybrid permutations. 3) Run a golden-traffic exercise during next canary to validate warmup for Private tenants. 4) Update runbook to explicitly include override steps and notification templates.
